pk.context: 1500 mg intravenous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear, colorless solution in a single-use vial

tell: Chemically unrelated to existing antiepileptic drugs, it binds the synaptic vesicle protein SV2A.

clues.text: Almost completely absorbed after oral dosing, and the injection is bioequivalent to tablets. Under 10% bound to plasma protein, and 66% of the dose is excreted unchanged by the kidneys.
A single enantiomer, crystalline powder with a molecular weight of 170.21 that is very soluble in water.
Approved under an NDA as 500 mg per 5 mL single-use vials that must be diluted before intravenous infusion.
Contraindicated with known hypersensitivity, as anaphylaxis and angioedema have occurred; no boxed warning. Somnolence and asthenia are the most common reactions.

Partial-onset seizures from 1 month of age; adjunctive therapy for myoclonic seizures in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy and for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures; intravenous when oral dosing is not feasible.
Binds the synaptic vesicle protein SV2A, thought to regulate vesicle exocytosis; the precise antiepileptic mechanism is unknown.
The generic name begins with L and has thirteen letters.
